Main.sentence: The Coptic cross is any of a number of ___E:Christian cross variants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_cross_variants)___ associated in some way with ___E:Coptic Christians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coptic_Christians)___ .
The typical form of the "Coptic cross" used in the Coptic Church is made up of two bold lines of equal length that intersect at the middle at right angles.
Each line terminates in three points, representing the ___E:Trinity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity)___ of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Altogether, the cross has 12 points symbolizing the Apostles, whose mission was to spread the Gospel message throughout the world.

This form of Coptic cross is widely used in the Coptic church and the ___E:Ethiopian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Orthodox_Tewahedo_Church)___ and ___E:Eritrean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Orthodox_Tewahedo_Church)___ churches, and so this form of the cross may also be called the " ___E:Ethiopian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Church)___ cross" or " ___E:Axum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Aksum)___ cross". [citation needed] Bertran de la Farge dates it to the 4th century and cites it as a predecessor of the ___E:Occitan cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_cross)___ .  [better source needed]

In 1984, a modern variant of the Coptic cross composed of three bars intersecting at right angles in three dimensions was given as a gift by the ___E:Coptic Orthodox Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coptic_Orthodox_Church)___ and mounted on the top of the ___E:All Africa Conference of Churches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Africa_Conference_of_Churches)___ building since the Coptic Church is considered to be the mother church in Africa.

Many ___E:Copts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copts)___ have the cross ___E:tattooed as a sign of faith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_perspectives_on_tattooing#Christianity)___ on the inside of their right arm at the wrist.
